context.hint: A Python connector's central formatter now has a generalized private-key span plus key-name authentication-code, authorization-scheme, and double-quoted cloud-key maskers. A 23-carrier pristine/patched matrix passed with benign controls, but the change has not been exported as a standalone diff, applied to a fresh copy, or checked against the repository's existing secret-detector test functions. Question: does the patch replay cleanly and preserve existing behavior and benign PEM-adjacent text?
context.surface: Python connector package with a central logging.Formatter applied to application and SDK handlers; disposable local logging fixtures; no live database or network required.
assumptions: The analyst can read the connector source and run a disposable local Python fixture with a writable temporary log.
The attacker controls credential strings and field values that reach debug logs, but not the formatter code or its composition order.
The formatter is attached to file or stream handlers in the real product; direct formatter invocation is an acceptable bounded proxy for a first probe.
No official host-side benchmark evaluator is available inside the local container.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: a real multiline private-key block survives because the PEM regex expects literal backslash-n separators and only a generic header. Applicability: the central formatter is attached to file logging, and the analyst may call it directly on a disposable string. Bounded test: emit generic, RSA, and ENCRYPTED blocks with real newlines and a base64 marker, plus a literal-backslash-n control. Expected result: base64 markers disappear and END headers remain; falsifier: any marker survives. Cleanup: delete the temporary log and fixture key material.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: the working-tree diff applies cleanly to a fresh pristine copy and reproduces every carrier outcome. Applicability: a disposable copy and a saved unified diff are available. Bounded test: run apply-check, apply the patch, compare the modified file with the working copy, and rerun the carrier matrix. Expected result: apply succeeds, files are byte-identical, and every masked/benign check matches; falsifier: a hunk rejects or any check flips. Cleanup: remove the replay copy and temporary logs.

Hypothesis: the patch does not regress existing secret-detector test functions. Applicability: the test modules can be loaded through a minimal package shim when optional connector dependencies are absent. Bounded test: execute every test function in the two secret-detector test files against pristine and patched copies. Expected result: all previously passing functions still pass; falsifier: any function fails after the patch or collection differs. Cleanup: delete both test work directories.

Hypothesis: a broad private-key span over-masks PEM-adjacent benign text such as public keys, SSH-known-host base64 lines, or prose mentioning an authentication-code field. Applicability: the formatter is run on disposable mixed-content logs. Bounded test: emit public-certificate and public-key blocks, a known-host base64 line, and prose containing passcode/otp words next to real code-key carriers. Expected result: only real secret carriers change; falsifier: a public block or benign base64 line is altered. Cleanup: delete the fixture log.

Hypothesis: formatter behavior differs when attached through the product's file-logging configuration rather than called directly. Applicability: an isolated process can configure a temporary file handler without opening a live connection. Bounded test: emit a private-key block and an authentication-code line through the connector logger namespace, then compare the file bytes with direct formatter output. Expected result: both paths mask identically; falsifier: the attached-handler output leaks a marker. Cleanup: remove handler files and reset logger state.

Hypothesis: serializer differences produce escaped-newline private-key carriers that a real-newline-only span misses. Applicability: the formatter receives JSON-serialized request data. Bounded test: emit the same private-key body through two serializers with different newline escaping and two randomized marker lengths. Expected result: both serialized forms lose the marker; falsifier: one serializer's body survives. Cleanup: delete serialized fixtures and logs.

evaluations.rationale: Selected: the strongest evidence base and the repair already exist; this round uses the incumbent to drive replay and regression rather than opening a new mechanism.
Highest-value closure check; deferred only because it is a verification action for the incumbent rather than a separate hypothesis.
Important compatibility signal, but lower feasibility because the local package import chain lacks optional dependencies.
Strong over-masking discriminator and easy to run alongside replay.
Useful wiring-level check, but heavier than the direct-formatter path used by the bounded probe.
Mechanism already covered by the escaped-newline carrier in the third iteration; retained as a lower-value randomized alternative.

observation.summary: The working-tree change was exported as a standalone unified diff. A fresh disposable copy passed apply-check and apply; the applied formatter file was byte-identical to the working copy. A replay probe produced identical output on both trees and passed 27/27 checks: all private-key shapes after replay, six authentication-code carriers, an authorization-scheme JWT, a double-quoted cloud-key secret, benign six-digit/zip text, public-certificate text, public-key text, and a known-host base64 line, plus every test function in the two repository secret-detector test files (ten log tests and four out-of-band tests). Evidence strength: patch replay plus repository-test replay with benign controls. Limits: tests ran through a minimal package shim because optional connector dependencies are absent; handler wiring was not separately exercised; the official host-side evaluator was not run, so the benchmark verdict remains unverified.
observation.next_hint: Run the official host-side evaluator on the exported patch JSONL. If it is unavailable, retain the local replay and regression evidence as unverified and report the environment blocker separately.
